## Add new "Getting Started with Traces" quickstart guide

We need a new quickstart guide that introduces users to Logs, Traces, and Metrics in Snowflake. The guide should walk through building a Notebook that pulls weather data from the OpenWeather REST API as part of a Medallion Architecture pipeline, demonstrating how to trace performance and retrieve memory/CPU information from a procedure and UDF execution.

    The guide should cover:
    - Creating a Notebook with Python and SQL cells
    - Building a Python UDF that fetches data from an external API
    - Creating a stored procedure to populate a bronze-level table
    - Enabling tracing at the database and schema level
    - Viewing and analyzing trace data

    Please ensure the quickstart is complete, accurate, and includes all necessary prerequisites, setup steps, and visual aids (screenshots) where helpful.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files to understand how the site is built and how quickstarts are structured:
    - `site/README.md` – overview of the site structure
    - `site/package.json` – npm scripts and dependencies for the site
    - `site/gulpfile.js` – build tasks for the site
    - `FORMAT-GUIDE.md` – formatting conventions for quickstart content
    - `site/sfguides/` – existing quickstart examples to reference for structure and style

## Implementation Plan
1. Create a new directory `site/sfguides/src/getting_started_with_traces/` to hold the quickstart content.
    2. Add a markdown file `getting_started_with_traces.md` with the full quickstart content, following the standard quickstart format (front matter with author, id, summary, categories, etc., followed by numbered sections with `Duration` metadata).
    3. Structure the guide with the following sections:
       - **Overview**: Describe what the user will learn and build (Logs, Traces, Metrics; OpenWeather API; Medallion Architecture).
       - **Prerequisites**: List what the user needs (Snowflake account with appropriate permissions, OpenWeather API key).
       - **Creating the Notebook**: Steps to create a warehouse, database, and schema with tracing enabled; create a Notebook in Snowsight.
       - **Setup**: First notebook cell with session setup and API key input via Streamlit widget.
       - **Network Configuration**: Configure network rule, secret, and external access integration.
       - **Creating the UDF**: Build a Python UDF that calls the OpenWeather API.
       - **Creating the Procedure**: Build a stored procedure that populates the bronze layer.
       - **Viewing Traces**: How to view trace data in Snowsight, including filtering by query ID or executable name.
       - **Custom Spans**: Add custom spans to showcase custom instrumentation (use span events instead of debug-level logging to work around potential UI representation issues).
       - **Conclusion / Summary**: Recap what was learned.
    4. Add a screenshot image `trace_details.png` to the `assets/` subdirectory illustrating trace details in the Snowsight UI.
    5. Ensure all code blocks are accurate and tested against the current Snowflake feature set.
    6. Review the guide for consistency with other quickstarts in the `site/sfguides/src/` directory, following formatting and style conventions.
I'll start by exploring the site structure and understanding how quickstarts are organized.

1: # Codelabs Site
2: 
3: A site for hosting codelabs content.
4: 
5: 
6: ## Prerequisites
7: 
8: The project requires the following major dependencies:
9: 
10: - [Go](https://golang.org/dl/) language
11: - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) v10+ and [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/get-npm)
12: - [gsutil](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/gsutil_install)
13: - [claat](https://github.com/googlecodelabs/tools/tree/master/claat#install)
14: 
15: With Node installed, run `npm install` in the root of the `site` (this folder):
16: 
17: ```text
18: $ npm install
19: ```
20: 
21: (Optional) npm installs binstubs at `./node_modules/.bin/`. When running tasks
22: like `gulp`, you may want to add `./node_modules/.bin/` to your `$PATH` for convenience:
23: 
24: ```text
25: $ export PATH="./node_modules/.bin/:$PATH"
26: ```
27: 
28: This does pose a mild security risk, so please do so at your own risk.
29: 
30: 
31: ## Development
32: 
33: ### Serve
34: 
35: To serve the site in dev mode, run `gulp serve`, passing a path to a directory
36: with the codelabs content as an argument. This will compile all the views and
37: codelabs into the `build/` directory and start a web server to serve that
38: content.
39: 
40: ```text
41: $ gulp serve
42: ```
43: 
44: The output will include the address where the server is running
45: (http://localhost:8000 by default).
46: 
47: You can also serve the completely compiled and minified (prod) version with the
48: `serve:dist` command. Always run this before publishing, as it will show you an
49: replica of what will appear on staging/production.
50: 
51: ```text
52: $ gulp serve:dist
53: ```
54: 
55: ### Views
56: 
57: Views are themed/styled collections of codelabs, served from the same url.
58: Codelab tags are used for selecting codelabs into views. View definitions are
59: stored in `/app/views` directory. Views commonly correspond to events (e.g. NEXT
60: 2018) or abstract themes (e.g. Windows), but we refer to them generically as
61: "views" internally.
62: 
63: #### Add a new view
64: 
65: To add a new view (e.g. to serve codelabs for a particular event):
66: 
67: 1. Create a new folder in `app/views`, which will be the "view id". As the view
68: id will appear in the URL, the name should be sluggified, meaning all lowercase
69: with special characters replaced with dashes.
70: 
71:     ```text
72:     // General example
73:     My Codelab -> my-codelab
74: 
75:     // Always substitute file extensions, otherwise the browser will get confused
76:     Learn underscore.js -> learn-underscore-js
77: 
78:     // Keep other URL-friendly characters when the context warrants
79:     Tracking with utm_source -> tracking-with-utm_source
80:     ```
81: 
82: 1. Add a new file named `view.json` inside this folder. Here is a template
83: `view.json`:
84: 
85:     ```javascript
86:     // app/views/my-event/view.json
87:     {
88:       // Required: page and view title.
89:       "title": "My Event",
90: 
91:       // Required: Text description of the event. This will appear in the view
92:       // landing page.
93:       "description": "",
94: 
95:       // Required: list of string tags by which to include codelabs. Tags are
96:       // specified in the codelab by the codelab author.
97:       "tags": [],
98: 
99:       // Optional: list of string categories by which to include codelabs.
100:       // Categories are specified in the codelab by the codelab author.
101:       "categories": [],
102: 
103:       // Optional: name of a custom stylesheet to include. See also: point below
104:       // about custom styles.
105:       "customStyle": "style.css",
106: 
107:       // Optional: list of regular expressions to exclude particular codelabs.
108:       "exclude": [],
109: 
110:       // Optional: URL to a custom logo for the codelab. If provided, this logo
111:       // must be placed in app/views/<view-id>/ and referenced as such. For
112:       // example, if the event was named "my-event", this logo would exist at
113:       // app/views/my-event/my-event-logo.svg.
114:       //
115:       // Where possible, please use SVG logos. When SVG logos are not available,
116:       // please size images to be 125px high at 72 DPI.
117:       //
118:       // Minify images before uploading using a tool like ImageOptim.
119:       "logoUrl": "/my-event/my-event-logo.svg",
120: 
121:       // Optional: category level to use for iconography
122:       "catLevel": 0,
123: 
124:       // Optional: Method for sorting codelabs.
125:       "sort": "mainCategory",
126: 
127:       // Optional: List of codelab IDs that should be "pinned" at the start.
128:       // This is useful for "getting started" codelabs or when users should
129:       // complete codelabs in a specific order.
130:       "pins": [],
131: 
132:       // Optional: custom google analytics tracking code. By default, all
133:       // codelab views are tracked on the main codelab analytics.
134:       "ga": "",
135: 
136:       // Optional: If true, do not include this view in the list of views on
137:       // the home page. It will still be accessible via the direct URL.
138:       "hidden": false,
139:     }
140:     ```
141: 
142: 1. (Optional) Add a file named `style.css` inside the view folder. If provided,
143: this file will be included in the HTML, allowing for custom styles.
144: 
145:     This file is not included in the main assets bundle, so there will be a
146:     performance decrease as the browser needs to load additional styles.
147:     Furthermore, if the codelab schema were to change, your custom styles may be
148:     broken. Please check with the codelabs team to see if your style changes
149:     make more sense to upstream across all views.
150: 
151: 1. (Optional) Add a file named `index.html` inside the view folder. This allows
152: you to fully customize the view, but comes at the expense of duplication. Please
153: use this sparingly and check with the core team before making drastic changes.
154: 
155: 1. Execute the `serve` command as described above to see the view.
156: 
157: #### Build and serve a single view (deprecated)
158: 
159: The build is very fast, so you should not need to filter by a specific view.
160: Instead, build all views and then visit the appropriate URL. If you still wish
161: to build a single set of views, you can do so with the `--views-filter`
162: parameter:
163: 
164: ```text
165: $ gulp serve --views-filter='^event-*'
166: ```
167: 
168: Note this filter takes a regular expression. By default, all views are built.
169: 
170: 
171: ## Deployment
172: 
173: Once you build, serve, and verify your labs, you're on your own for publishing the artifacts. There are many ways to publish a static web site and we won't try to cover them all, however, we have included support for deploying your landing pages and codelabs to Google Cloud Storage (GCS).
174: 
175: ### Setup for GCS Support
176: 
177: #### Set  environment variables like this (use your own names):
178: 
179: ```
180: export STAGING_BUCKET=gs://mco-codelabs-staging
181: export PROD_BUCKET=gs://mco-codelabs-prod
182: ```
183: 
184: #### Create staging and production buckets like this (use your own names):
185: 
186: ```
187: 18:42:32 site$ gsutil mb is $STAGING_BUCKET
188: Creating gs://mco-codelabs-staging/...
189: 18:42:47 site$ gsutil mb $PROD_BUCKET
190: Creating gs://mco-codelabs-prod/...
191: ```
192: 
193: #### Setup permissions and web access to your buckets
194: 
195: 1. Make newly uploaded files world-readable and ensure user@ has owner
196: permissions:
197: 
198:     ```text
199:     $ gsutil defacl ch -g all:R -u you@your-domain.com:O $STAGING_BUCKET $PROD_BUCKET
200:     $ gsutil iam ch allUsers:objectViewer $STAGING_BUCKET $PROD_BUCKET
201:     ```
202: 
203:     Add as many `-u user@` as you require. This ensures the users will remain
204:     owners no matter who updates your bucket.
205: 
206: ### Deploy to staging
207: 
208: The following commands perform a "copy" operation, uploading all local files to
209: the staging bucket. The local copy of a file will overwrite the staging copy of
210: the same file. Staging files that do not exist in the local copy will be
211: untouched. To perform a complete "sync" (make staging look exactly like the
212: local copy), specify `--delete-missing` on the publish command.
213: 
214: 1. Compile and minify the build:
215: 
216:     ```text
217:     $ gulp dist
218:     ```
219: 
220: 1. Deploy views to the staging bucket:
221: 
222:     ```text
223:     $ gulp publish:staging:views --staging-bucket=$STAGING_BUCKET
224:     ```
225: 
226: 1. Deploy codelabs to the staging bucket:
227: 
228:     ```text
229:     $ gulp publish:staging:codelabs --staging-bucket=$STAGING_BUCKET
230:     ```
231: 
232: 1. Visit the [staging site](https://mco-codelabs-staging.storage.googleapis.com/index.html) (modify link to match your staging bucket name).
233: 
234: See [#options](#options) for information on how to customize the staging bucket.
235: 
236: ### Deploy to prod
237: 
238: We do not deploy from local to production. Instead, we "promote" a staging build
239: to production.
240: 
241: The following commands perform a "copy" operation, uploading all staging files
242: to the prod bucket. The staging copy of a file will overwrite the prod copy of
243: the same file. Prod files that do not exist in the staging bucket will be
244: untouched. To perform a complete "sync" (make prod look exactly like staging),
245: specify `--delete-missing` on the publish command.
246: 
247: 1. Deploy views from the staging bucket to the production bucket:
248: 
249:     ```text
250:     $ gulp publish:prod:views --staging-bucket=$STAGING_BUCKET --prod-bucket=$PROD_BUCKET
251:     ```
252: 
253: 1. Deploy codelabs from the staging bucket to the production bucket:
254: 
255:     ```text
256:     $ gulp publish:prod:codelabs --staging-bucket=$STAGING_BUCKET --prod-bucket=$PROD_BUCKET
257:     ```
258: 
259: 1. Visit the [production site](https://mco-codelabs-prod.storage.googleapis.com/index.html)  (modify link to match your production bucket name).
260: 
261: See [#options](#options) for information on how to customize the staging and
262: prod bucket.
263: 
264: ### Deploy to custom bucket
265: 
266: This section describes the steps to create and deploy to a custom bucket.
267: Replace `gs://codelabs.mycompany.com` with the name of your bucket. If you want
268: to use GCS directly for serving, the bucket name **must** be a valid domain.
269: 
270: 1. Create a new bucket:
271: 
272:     ```text
273:     $ gsutil mb gs://codelabs.mycompany.com
274:     ```
275: 
276: 1. Make newly uploaded files world-readable and ensure user@ has owner
277: permissions:
278: 
279:     ```text
280:     $ gsutil defacl ch -g all:R -u you@your-domain.com:O gs://codelabs.mycompany.com
281:     $ gsutil iam ch allUsers:objectViewer gs://codelabs.mycompany.com
282:     ```
283: 
284:     Add as many `-u user@` as you require. This ensures the users will remain
285:     owners no matter who updates your bucket.
286: 
287: 1. Set the default main page suffix and not found page:
288: 
289:     ```text
290:     $ gsutil web set -m index.html -e 404.html gs://codelabs.mycompany.com
291:     ```
292: 
293:     This option is only available on bucket names that are valid domains.
294: 
295: 
296: Follow the steps in [deploy to staging](#deploy-to-staging) with a custom
297: `--staging-bucket` parameter. See [#options](#options) for information.
298: 
299: 
300: ### Deploy single view or codelab
301: 
302: Where possible, build and publish the entire website. This will ensure all
303: assets are up-to-date.
304: 
305: To build and publish a set of views to staging:
306: 
307: ```text
308: $ gulp dist --views-filter=^my-event
309: $ gulp publish:staging:views
310: ```
311: 
312: To build and publish a set of codelabs to staging:
313: 
314: ```text
315: $ gulp dist --codelabs-filter=^my-codelab
316: $ gulp publish:staging:codelabs
317: ```
318: 
319: ## Options
320: 
321: `--base-url` - base URL for serving canonical links. This should always include
322: the protocol (http:// or https://) and NOT including a trailing slash. The
323: default value is "https://codelabs.developers.google.com".
324: 
325: `--codelabs-dir` - absolute or relative path on disk where codelabs are stored.
326: Any filters will be applied to these codelabs, and then the resulting selection
327: is symlinked into the build folder. The default value is "." (the current directory).
328: 
329: `--codelabs-filter` - regular expression by which to filter codelabs IDs for
330: inclusion. If a filter is not specified, all codelabs are included.
331: 
332: `--codelabs-namespace` - URL path where codelabs will be served in the web
333: server. The default value is "/codelabs", meaning codelabs will be served at
334: https://URL/codelabs.
335: 
336: `--dry` - Print out steps instead of actually taking them. This only applies  to
337: publish operations.
338: 
339: `--delete-missing` - Delete any files in the destination that are not present
340: at the source (rsync-style behavior).
341: 
342: `--prod-bucket` - name of the GCS bucket to use for production resources. This
343: is only used for publishing.
344: 
345: `--staging-bucket` - name of the GCS bucket to use for staging resources. This
346: is only used for publishing.
347: 
348: `--views-filter` - regular expression by which to filter included views
349: (events). If a filter is not specified, all views are included.
350: 
351: The following options are only relevant when invoking claat:
352: 
353: `--codelabs-env` - environment for which to build codelabs. The default value is
354: "web".
355: 
356: `--codelabs-format` - format in which to build the codelabs. The default value
357: is "html"
358: 
359: `--codelab-source` - Google Doc ID from which to build codelab. This can be
360: specified multiple times to build from multiple sources.
361: 
362: 
363: ## Testing
364: 
365: To run the tests manually in a browser, execute the following:
366: 
367: ```text
368: $ gulp serve
369: $ open http://localhost:8000/app/js/all_tests.html
370: ```
371: 
372: 
373: ## Help
374: 
375: For help documentation/usage of the Gulp tasks, run:
376: 
377: ```text
378: $ gulp -T
379: ```
380: 
381: If gulp startup times are really slow, try removing `node_modules/` or running
382: 
383: ```text
384: $ npm dedupe
385: ```

(End of file - total 385 lines)
</content>

1: # Codelab Formatting Guide
2: 
3: Bug or feature request? File it [here](https://github.com/googlecodelabs/tools/issues).
4: 
5: ## Getting Started
6: 
7: Copy [this template doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1E6XMcdTexh5O8JwGy42SY3Ehzi8gOfUGiqTiUX6N04o/edit) as a starting point and then iteratively mutate the metadata and contents to your liking, following the formatting rules described below.
8: 
9: To preview a codelab:
10: 
11: -  (optional one-time setup) Install the [Preview Codelab Chrome extension](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/preview-codelab/lhojjnijnkiglhkggagbapfonpdlinji) in your browser.
12: 
13: - Click the Chrome extension's button while you're in your codelab Google Doc tab, or
14: - Navigate manually to **https://codelabs-preview.appspot.com/?file_id=[google-doc-id]**.
15: 
16: ## Formatting Reference
17: 
18: 1. Table of Contents
19: 
20:     Every codelab document must use the **Heading 1** paragraph style to delineate the steps of the codelab. In turn, these headings will be used to automatically create a Table of Contents which shows the student exactly where they are in the codelab and lets them jump to any step.
21: 
22:     The table of contents disappears for smaller browsers but is still available from the hamburger menu.
23: 
24: 1. Codelab Metadata (Google Docs)
25: 
26:     There is some additional metadata that is required in order to properly publish a codelab. This metadata should be added as a **two-column table** anywhere before the first step of the codelab. For example:
27: 
28: 
29: 
30:     You are free to add your own metadata here if you'd like but certain key/value pairs are reserved for specific codelab publishing features. The current list of reserved metadata terms are:
31: 
32:     * **Summary:** A short summary of the codelab that will be shown in the codelab browser UI.
33:     * **URL:** The URL suffix where this codelab will be published, i.e. the path after the root URL to a collection of codelabs. For example, the Google Codelabs site uses codelabs.developers.google.com/codelabs/ as root and this value is appended to that base to form the unique URL for a given codelab.
34:     * **Category:** A single, top-level category that will be used to group codelabs by platform. Categories are normally curated by an organization (e.g. we have a set we use for the Google Codelabs site) but each publisher is free to use this value at their discretion.
35:     * **Environment**: A tag that allows use to output some codelabs for a specific environment. All codelabs default to the "Web" environment but given some hardware constraints we might only want to generate them for a "Kiosk" environment where we know people will have the right hardware. \
36: You can also use this to target specific events, for instance:  \
37: "Web, polymer-summit" (without quotes)
38:     * **Status:** One or more of (Draft, Published, Deprecated, Hidden) to indicate the progress and whether the codelab is ready to be published. 'Hidden' implies the codelab is for restricted use, should be available only by direct URL, and should not appear on the main index page.
39:     * **Feedback Link:** The URL that the student should be sent to when they click on the feedback link to report a bug in the codelab.
40:     * **Analytics Account:** This allows you to specify a custom Google Analytics ID for your codelab. If no ID is specified, it defaults to a global codelabs analytics account.
41: 
42: 1. Codelab Metadata (Markdown)
43: 
44:     You are free to add your own metadata here if you'd like but certain key/value pairs are reserved for specific codelab publishing features. The current list of reserved metadata terms are:
45: 
46:     * **summary:** A short summary of the codelab that will be shown in the codelab browser UI.
47:     * **id:** The name of the folder that will be generated once you export the markdown file via claat.
48:     * **categories:** A single, top-level category that will be used to group codelabs by platform. Categories are normally curated by an organization (e.g. we have a set we use for the Google Codelabs site) but each publisher is free to use this value at their discretion.
49:     * **environments**: A tag that allows use to output some codelabs for a specific environment. All codelabs default to the "Web" environment but given some hardware constraints we might only want to generate them for a "Kiosk" environment where we know people will have the right hardware. \
50: You can also use this to target specific events, for instance:  \
51: "Web, polymer-summit" (without quotes)
52:     * **status:** One or more of (Draft, Published, Deprecated, Hidden) to indicate the progress and whether the codelab is ready to be published. 'Hidden' implies the codelab is for restricted use, should be available only by direct URL, and should not appear on the main index page.
53:     * **feedback link:** The URL that the student should be sent to when they click on the feedback link to report a bug in the codelab.
54:     * **analytics account:** This allows you to specify a custom Google Analytics ID for your codelab. If no ID is specified, it defaults to a global codelabs analytics account.
55:     * **tags:** Add relevant tags to make your codelab easily found.
56:     * **authors:** Indicate the author(s) of this specific codelab.
57: 
58: 1. Headers
59: 
60:     Within the steps of your codelab you should use the **Heading 2**, **Heading 3** and **Heading 4** paragraph styles to organize your content. These will get translated to `<h2>`, `<h3>` and `<h4>` tags in the codelab markup.
61: 
62:     Also, if you wish to include some additional administrative information at the beginning of your codelab you can freely use the **Heading 2**, **Heading 3** and **Heading 4** paragraph styles and they will not show up in the codelab as long as they appear before the first **Heading 1**.
63: 
64: 1. Text Styles
65: 
66:     For the most part, it doesn't matter which fonts you use in your Google Doc draft; everything will be formatted using Roboto in the final codelab.
67: 
68:     There are some simple ways that you can add emphasis to certain parts of the text. Bolded and italicized text will be passed through to the codelab markup as `<strong>` and `<em>` tags respectively. Also, passages of text formatted with the `Courier New` font will be passed through as an inline `<code>` tag in the markup.
69: 
70: 1. Responsive Images
71: 
72:     Inline images in your codelab should just work seamlessly. You can re-size them in your codelab document and that width will be applied as a **max-width** on the image in the codelab markup so that images are the same size relative to the text but also scale down appropriately for smaller browsers.
73: 
74: 1. Youtube Videos
75: 
76:     Youtube Videos can be embedded by doing:
77:      - Add an image in the document. The image can be a screenshot of the video for instance but it doesn't really matter since it won't be displayed but replaced by the embedded video.
78:      - Add an "Alt Text" to the image by doing **Cmd+Opt+Y** or **Right click > "Alt Text..."**
79:      - Put a Youtube video link in the **Description** field of the Alt Text. in the format `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=[video_ID]`
80:     > Specifying a start time is not supported at this time.
81: 
82: 1. Embedded Iframes
83: 
84:     Iframes can be embedded by doing:
85:      - Add an image in the document. The image can be a screenshot of the iframe for instance but it doesn't really matter since it won't be displayed but replaced by the embedded iframe.
86:      - Add an "Alt Text" to the image by doing **Cmd+Opt+Y** or **Right click > "Alt Text..."**
87:      - Put a full URL in the **Description** field of the Alt Text. in the format `https://www.domain.com/watch?foo=bar`. Note that for security reasons, iframe embbedding is limited to an enumerated set of allowable iframe source URLs. Feel free to submit a PR if you'd like to augment that list or tweak your own version of the claat command.
88: 
89: 1. Info Boxes
90: 
91:     For additional information that you would like to specially call-out in your codelab, there are two styles of info boxes:
92: 
93:     1. Positive information like best practices and time saving tips should be formatted as a **single-cell table** with a **light green 3** background.
94: 
95:     2. Negative information like warnings and API usage restrictions should be formatted as a **single-cell table** with a **light orange 3** background.
96: 
97:     It is recommended that you keep your infoboxes clean, concise and focused on a single topic. If you have information which may be useful to know but is not a critical part of the codelab instructions, then you should link to that information from the FAQ section rather than including it as an infobox.
98: 
99: 1. Command-line Snippets
100: 
101:     It's often the case that you will have command-line instructions or log messages which are formatted with a monospaced font and have pre-defined whitespace. You can add these sections to your codelab by creating a **single-cell table** and making sure that all the text is formatted using the **Consolas font**.
102: 
103: 1. Code Snippets
104: 
105:     Code snippets with syntax highlighting can be added by creating a **single-cell table** and making sure that all the text is formatted using the **`Courier New`** font.
106: 
107:     Any additional styles applied to the code will be overridden by the syntax highlighting. This means that you're free to use code highlighting Add-ons in your codelab doc but it will have no effect on how the code is highlighted in the final codelab.
108: 
109:     It is also strongly recommended that you provide a **Heading 3** header directly above your code snippet with the file name. This helps students keep track of where the code is coming from. The codelab framework also uses the file extension of the prior header as a clue for how to highlight the code.
110: 
111:     It is also strongly recommended that you make your **Heading 3** header a hyperlink to the actual file if it is available on GitHub. A GitHub icon will automatically be added to the heading in such cases.
112: 
113: 1. Frequently Asked Questions
114: 
115:     As the author of the codelab, you have developed and tested your code. You've probably run into all sorts of common issues or misconceptions. By linking to frequently asked questions, after each step where they often occur, you will reassure the students that they have everything they need to complete the codelab and avoid having to explain everything inline in your codelab.
116:     FAQs are easy to add. All the author needs to do is provide an unordered list of hyperlinks and preface it with a **Heading 3** header with the exact text: **Frequently Asked Questions**.
117: 
118:     Link icons will be added automatically for stackoverflow.com, developers.google.com, developers.android.com and support.google.com. All links will be configured to open in a new tab.
119: 
120: 1. Download Buttons
121: 
122:     You can make it really easy to get started by including direct download buttons inline in your codelab. In order to add a button to your codelab, simply add a hyperlink and make sure that it is highlighted with a **dark green 1** background.
123: 
124:     Additionally, if the link text begins with the word "Download", a file download icon will be added to the button.
125: 
126: 1. Per-step Time Estimates
127: 
128:     Many participants are not fully committed to completing a codelab when they start it. One of the ways that we can keep them in our codelab is by giving them accurate estimates about how much additional effort is required to complete the codelab at each step.
129: 
130:     In order to add this feature to your codelab, simply annotate each step in your codelab doc with a Duration: which uses **dark grey 1** text.
131: 
132:     That's it. The codelab framework will do everything else for you. If you forget to annotate a step with a duration, the default is 1:00. Also, if the last step of your codelab is just a congratulations page, you should set the duration of that step to **0**.
133: 
134: 1. Conditional Steps
135: 
136:     Sometimes it's useful to have different versions of a codelab for different environments. For example, you might have some steps that only apply to students who take the codelab in a classroom setting while other steps only apply to people who are following the instructions at their own pace online.
137: 
138:     The format is similar to the duration metadata. You simply specify one or more environments with an Environment: which uses **dark grey 1** text. The Duration and/or Environment fields, when present, should be followed by a blank line and should be set in normal text (not in Heading 1, lest they be considered part of the step title).
139: 
140:     If no environment metadata is specified, the default environment is "Web, Kiosk".
141: 
142:     When previewing your codelab, you can change environments using the &env=web or &env=kiosk parameters.
143: 
144: 1. Fragment imports
145: 
146:     It is possible for a codelab to import another doc as a step fragment. For instance, it could be a set of setup instructions shared among multiple codelabs:
147: 
148:     [[**import** [funny dog](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VkJopEKiqitwFgqFOEU6rpB1VE-R-uYWq4erNHP2TQ4/edit)]]
149: 
150:     The contents of the funny dog document will be inserted in the codelab, replacing import instruction.
151: 
152:     The instruction syntax is:
153: 
154:     *   start with [[ (two square brackets)
155:     *   followed by **import** keyword in bold
156:     *   followed by a link to a doc
157:     *   end with ]] (two square brackets)
158: 
159:     Caveat: The imported doc is limited to content within a step (hence the term "fragment"). Including multiple steps, or even the step title/heading, within the imported doc is not supported.
160: 
161: 1. Resumable Codelabs
162: 
163:     When a user returns to a codelab, they may be returning via a bookmark or a short-link posted online, it usually takes them to the first page of the codelab. In that case, the codelab remembers where they left off and asks them if they wish to resume where they left off. This makes it easier for the user to jump back in and gives us more accurate analytics about how long users spend on each step.
164: 
165:     This is simply part of the framework. There is nothing that you need to do as a codelab author to enable this feature.
166: 
167: 1. Feedback Links
168: 
169:     At the bottom of every step of the codelab there is a link for reporting bugs. This link can be configured using the **Feedback Link** setting in your metadata table.
170: 
171: 1. Inline Surveys
172: 
173:     **NOTE: Surveys cannot be used to collect data that can individually, or in conjunction with other information from this site, help locate and identify a particular user or reveal their sensitive demographics information. Any data collected should be sufficiently anonymized and aggregated. Also, consider that the surveys can possibly send a numerical ID of the selections instead of the actual value itself. Apart from helping on the localization front, this can also help prevent from injecting obvious PII values into GA.**
174: 
175:     As we've seen in previous years, participants consume our codelabs for a wide range of reasons. In order to give us some more insight into how different people consume codelabs, we can ask them some quick multiple choice questions in the early stages of our codelab.
176: 
177:     You can configure these short survey questions to ask whatever you think is relevant to your codelab. In order to include a survey question in your codelab, add a single-cell table with a **light blue 3** background. Format your question with the **Heading 4** paragraph style and provide an **unordered list** of choices.
178: 
179:     The participants' answers will automatically be added as custom variables in Google Analytics which can help you understand things like:
180: 
181:     *   _What is the difference in completion rate between novices and experts?_
182:     *   _What is the average time spent for people who wanted to write code vs. people who just wanted to read?_
183:     *   _Is the bounce rate affected by the students' preference in IDE?_
184: 
185:     Of course, we need to be mindful of our participants' time and concentration and only ask a few key questions. It is _not_ recommended to have a survey after each step.
186: 
187: 1. What you'll learn
188: 
189:     Having a header 2 of "What you'll learn" followed by a bullet point list creates a list of check marks.
190: 
191:     A title of "What we've covered" has the same effect.
192:     
193: 1. YouTube Video Embeds
194: 
195:     Use a video tag like so `<video id="DWAinkJ54AP8"></video>` to embed a video uploaded to YouTube with the URL https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DWAinkJ54AP8
196: 
197: ## Things to avoid
198: 
199: - **Footers:** Any characters included in the footer (beyond the default page number) result in parsing bugs. For this reason, page footers are not recommended.

432: // gulpdebug is a helper for debugging gulp pipeline transforms. It logs the
433: // file path and then invokes the callback.

441: // run executes the given command with the specified arguments.
442: const run = (cmd, args, callback) => {
443:   const proc = spawn(cmd, args, { stdio: 'inherit' });
444:   proc.on('close', callback);

447: // parseViewMetadata parses the metadata of a single view and returns that metadata
448: // as JSON.
449: const parseViewMetadata = (filepath) => {
450:   if (path.basename(filepath) !== 'view.json') {
451:     throw new Error(`can only be called on view.json, got: ${filepath}`);
452:   }
453: 
454:   const dirname = path.dirname(filepath);
455:   const meta = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filepath));
456: 
457:   meta.id = path.basename(dirname);
458:   meta.url = viewFilename(meta.id).replace(/\.html$/, '');
459: 
460:   if (meta.sort === undefined) {
461:     meta.sort = meta.id === 'default' ? 'mainCategory' : 'title';
462:   }
463: 
464:   if (fs.existsSync(path.resolve(dirname, 'style.css'))) {
465:     meta.customStyle = `/${meta.id}/style.css`;
466:   }
467: 
468:   const defMeta = defaultViewMetadata();
469:   for (let key in defMeta) {
470:     if (meta[key] === undefined) {
471:       meta[key] = defMeta[key];
472:     }
473:   }
474: 
475:   return meta;
476: }
477: 
478: // parseCodelabMetadata parses the codelab metadata at the given path.
479: const parseCodelabMetadata = (filepath) => {
480:   var meta = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(filepath));
481: 
482:   meta.category = meta.category || [];
483:   if (!Array.isArray(meta.category)) {
484:     meta.category = [meta.category];
485:   }
486: 
487:   meta.mainCategory = meta.category[0] || DEFAULT_CATEGORY;
488:   meta.categoryClass = categoryClass(meta);
489:   meta.url = path.join(CODELABS_NAMESPACE, meta.id, 'index.html');
490: 
491:   return meta;
492: }
493: 
494: // defaultViewMetadata returns the default view metadata. This is cached for
495: // performance.
496: let _defaultViewMetadata;
497: const defaultViewMetadata = () => {
498:   if (!_defaultViewMetadata) {
499:     _defaultViewMetadata = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(DEFAULT_VIEW_META_PATH));
500:     _defaultViewMetadata.id = 'default';
501:     _defaultViewMetadata.url = viewFilename('default');
502:     _defaultViewMetadata.catLevel = 0;
503:     delete _defaultViewMetadata.ga;
504:   }
505:   return _defaultViewMetadata;
506: }
507: 
508: 
509: // Parse view.json and codelab.json files in all directories. Value returned in
510: // the callback is an object:
511: //
512: //     {
513: //       views: Object.<String, ViewObj>,
514: //       codelabs: Array.<CodelabObj>,
515: //       categories: Array.<String>
516: //     }
517: //
518: // Both codelabs and categories are sorted alphabetically. Codelabs are sorted
519: // by main category.
520: let _allMetadata;
521: const collectMetadata = () => {
522:   if (_allMetadata === undefined) {
523:     let codelabs = [];
524:     let categories = {};
525:     let views = {};
526: 
527:     const viewFiles = glob.sync('app/views/*/view.json');
528:     for (let i = 0; i < viewFiles.length; i++) {
529:       const view = parseViewMetadata(viewFiles[i]);
530:       views[view.id] = view;
531:     }
532: 
533:     const codelabFiles = glob.sync(`${CODELABS_BUILD_DIR}/*/codelab.json`);
534:     for (let i = 0; i < codelabFiles.length; i++) {
535:       const codelab = parseCodelabMetadata(codelabFiles[i]);
536:       codelabs.push(codelab);
537:       categories[codelab.mainCategory] = true;
538:     }
539: 
540:     _allMetadata = {
541:       categories: Object.keys(categories).sort(),
542:       codelabs: codelabs,
543:       views: views,
544:     }
545:   }
546: 
547:   return _allMetadata;
548: }

550: // generateDirectoryIndex accepts a stream of HTML files and converts them to
551: // directory indexes for use on a webserver. For example:
552: //
553: //    foo.html => foo/index.html
554: //
555: // Then the server can be configured to serve indexes and /foo will render
556: // properly.
557: const generateDirectoryIndex = () => {
558:   return through.obj((file, enc, callback) => {
559:     const srcPath = file.path;
560:     if (srcPath.match(/\.html$/) && fs.existsSync(srcPath)) {
561:       const dstPath = srcPath.replace(/\.html$/, '') + '/index.html';
562:       const dstPathDir = path.dirname(dstPath);
563:       const srcPathRel = path.relative(dstPathDir, srcPath);
564: 
565:       // Ensure directory exists
566:       fs.mkdirpSync(dstPathDir);
567: 
568:       // Change into the directory and create a relative symlink
569:       chdir(dstPathDir, () => {
570:         fs.ensureSymlinkSync(srcPathRel, 'index.html');
571:       });
572:     }
573:     callback(null, file);
574:   });
575: }
576: 
577: const chdir = (dir, callback) => {
578:   const cwd = process.cwd();
579:   process.chdir(dir);
580:   callback()
581:   process.chdir(cwd);
582: }
583: 
584: // generateView creates an index for the given view and codelabs data.
585: const generateView = () => {
586:   return through.obj((file, enc, callback) => {
587:     // viewId is the basename of the dirname of the event (e.g.
588:     // app/views/my-event/view.json -> my-event).
589:     const viewId = path.basename(path.dirname(file.path));
590: 
591:     // Read the HTML template for this view (or the default template if no
592:     // view-specific one exists).
593:     let templatePath = `app/views/${viewId}/index.html`;
594:     if (!fs.existsSync(templatePath)) {
595:       templatePath = DEFAULT_VIEW_TMPL_PATH;
596:     }
597:     const template = fs.readFileSync(templatePath);
598: 
599:     // Get the metadata about this view.
600:     const view = parseViewMetadata(file.path);
601: 
602:     // Aanalytics information.
603:     const ga = DEFAULT_GA;
604: 
605:     // Full list of views
606:     const all = collectMetadata();
607: 
608:     // Calculate URL parameters to append.
609:     let codelabUrlParams = 'index=' + encodeURIComponent('../..' + view.url);
610:     if (view.ga || args.indexGa) {
611:       let viewGa = args.indexGa ? args.indexGa : view.ga;
612:       codelabUrlParams += '&viewga=' + viewGa;
613:     }
614: 
615:     // Get the list of codelabs and categories for this view
616:     const filtered = filterCodelabs(view, all.codelabs);
617:     const codelabs = filtered.codelabs;
618:     const categories = filtered.categories;
619: 
620:     let locals = {
621:       baseUrl: BASE_URL,
622:       categories: categories,
623:       codelabs: codelabs,
624:       ga: ga,
625:       showcats: categories.length > 1,
626:       view: view,
627:       views: all.views,
628: 
629:       canonicalViewUrl: viewFuncs.canonicalViewUrl(),
630:       categoryClass: viewFuncs.categoryClass(),
631:       categoryHasShowableCodelabs: viewFuncs.categoryHasShowableCodelabs(viewId),
632:       codePrettyDate: viewFuncs.codelabPrettyDate(),
633:       codelabPin: viewFuncs.codelabPin(),
634:       codelabUrl: viewFuncs.codelabUrl(codelabUrlParams),
635:       levelledCategory: viewFuncs.levelledCategory(),
636:     };
637: 
638:     const html = swig.render(template.toString(), { locals: locals });
639:     file.contents = new Buffer.from(html);
640:     file.base = __dirname;
641:     file.path = viewFilename(viewId);
642: 
643:     callback(null, file);
644:   });
645: }
646: 
647: // viewFuncs is the list of functions shared by views (usually for rendering).
648: // This is a constant for performance instead of defining the functions inline.
649: const viewFuncs = {
650:   // categoryClass returns the top-level categoryClass function.
651:   categoryClass: () => {
652:     return categoryClass;
653:   },
654: 
655:   // canonicalViewUrl returns the canonical URL to the given view.
656:   canonicalViewUrl: () => {
657:     return (view) => {
658:       if (view.id === 'default' || view.id === '') {
659:         return `${BASE_URL}/`;
660:       }
661:       return `${BASE_URL}/${view.id}/`;
662:     };
663:   },
664: 
665:   // categoryHasShowableCodelabs returns true if the given category is present
666:   // in any of the given codelabs, or false otherwise.
667:   categoryHasShowableCodelabs: (viewId) => {
668:     return (category, codelabs) => {
669:       const codelabsUsingCategory = codelabs
670:         .filter((codelab) => {
671:           return codelab.category.indexOf(category) !== -1;
672:         })
673:         .filter((codelab) => {
674:           // Filter hidden codelabs from the default view. All other views are
675:           // explictly opt-in via metadata.
676:           return viewId !== 'default' || codelab.status.indexOf('hidden') === -1;
677:         });
678: 
679:       return codelabsUsingCategory.length > 0;
680:     }
681:   },
682: 
683:   // codelabPin returns the index of the pinned item, if it exists.
684:   codelabPin: () => {
685:     return (view, codelab) => {
686:       const i = view.pins.indexOf(codelab.id);
687:       if (i >= 0) {
688:         return i + 1;
689:       }
690:       return '';
691:     }
692:   },
693: 
694:   // codelabUrl returns the url for this codelab, combined with any additional
695:   // parameters if given.
696:   codelabUrl: (params) => {
697:     return (view, codelab) => {
698:       let url = codelab.url;
699:       if (params !== undefined) {
700:         url = `${url}?${params}`;
701:       }
702:       if (url.length > 0 && url[0] !== '/') {
703:         url = `/${url}`;
704:       }
705:       return url;
706:     }
707:   },
708: 
709:   // codelabPrettyDate returns a pretty-formatted date for the codelab view
710:   // page.
711:   codelabPrettyDate: () => {
712:     return (ts) => {
713:       const monthNames = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
714:       const d = new Date(ts);
715:       const month = monthNames[d.getMonth()];
716:       const date = d.getUTCDate();
717:       const year = d.getFullYear();
718: 
719:       return `${month} ${date}, ${year}`;
720:     }
721:   },
722: 
723:   // levelledCategory returns the levelledCategory top-level function.
724:   levelledCategory: () => {
725:     return levelledCategory;
726:   },
727: };
728: 
729: // viewFilename returns the view index file name based on provided view.
730: const viewFilename = (view) => {
731:   if (view === 'default') {
732:     return 'index.html';
733:   }
734:   return `${view}.html`;
735: }
736: 
737: // levelledCategory returns the codelab category level and name. If no category
738: // exists at that level, the nearest is returned. If the codelab has no
739: // categories, the default category and level 0 are returned.
740: const levelledCategory = (codelab, level) => {
741:   let i;
742:   for (i = level; i >= 0; i--) {
743:     var name = codelab.category[i];
744:     if (name) {
745:       break;
746:     }
747:   }
748:   if (!name) {
749:     name = DEFAULT_CATEGORY;
750:   }
751:   return { name: name, level: i };
752: }
753: 
754: // categoryClass converts the codelab to its corresponding CSS class.
755: const categoryClass = (codelab, level) => {
756:   var name = codelab.mainCategory;
757:   if (level > 0) {
758:     name += ' ' + codelab.category[level];
759:   }
760:   return name.toLowerCase().replace(/\s/g, '-');
761: }
762: 
763: // Filters out codelabs which do not match view spec. Currently, the matching is
764: // done by intersecting view.tags with each codelab.tags, and view.categories
765: // with codelab.category. All codelabs are matched if the view.tags and
766: // view.categories are empty.
767: //
768: // Additionally, each codelab is tested against view.exclude exclusion filters,
769: // matching codelab ID, status, tags and categories.
770: const filterCodelabs = (view, codelabs) => {
771:   var vtags = cleanStringList(view.tags);
772:   var vcats = cleanStringList(view.categories);
773: 
774:   // Filter out codelabs with tags that don't intersect with view.tags
775:   // unless view.tags is empty - equivalent to any tag.
776:   // Same for categories.
777:   codelabs = codelabs.filter(function(codelab) {
778:     // Matches by default if both tags and cats are empty.
779:     var match = !vtags.length && !vcats.length;
780:     var ctags = cleanStringList(codelab.tags);
781:     var ccats = cleanStringList(codelab.category);
782:     // Match by tags.
783:     if (vtags.length) {
784:       for (var i = 0; i < ctags.length; i++) {
785:         if (vtags.indexOf(ctags[i]) > -1) {
786:           match = true;
787:           break;
788:         }
789:       }
790:     }
791:     // Match by category.
792:     if (!match && vcats.length) {
793:       for (var i = 0; i < ccats.length; i++) {
794:         if (vcats.indexOf(ccats[i]) > -1) {
795:           match = true;
796:           break;
797:         }
798:       }
799:     }
800:     if (!match || !view.exclude.length) {
801:       return match;
802:     }
803:     // Tag or category matches. Test the exclusion filter.
804:     var cstatus = cleanStringList(codelab.status);
805:     for (var i = 0; i < view.exclude.length; i++) {
806:       var rex = view.exclude[i];
807:       if (codelab.id.match(rex)) {
808:         return false;
809:       }
810:       for (var j = 0; j < cstatus.length; j++) {
811:         if (cstatus[j].match(rex)) {
812:           return false;
813:         }
814:       }
815:       for (var j = 0; j < ctags.length; j++) {
816:         if (ctags[j].match(rex)) {
817:           return false;
818:         }
819:       }
820:       for (var j = 0; j < ccats.length; j++) {
821:         if (ccats[j].match(rex)) {
822:           return false;
823:         }
824:       }
825:     }
826:     return true;
827:   });
828: 
829:   // Compute distinct categories.
830:   var categories = {};
831:   for (var i in codelabs) {
832:     var cat = levelledCategory(codelabs[i], view.catLevel);
833:     categories[cat.name] = true;
834:   }
835: 
836:   // sort the codelabs.
837:   sortCodelabs(codelabs, view);
838: 
839:   return {
840:     codelabs: codelabs,
841:     categories: Object.keys(categories).sort(),
842:   };
843: }
844: 
845: 
846: // cleanStringList removes empty elements and converts the rest to lower case.
847: // The a argument is an array of strings or null/undefined. Alternatively, the
848: // argument can be a string of JSON-serialized array form.
849: const cleanStringList = (a) => {
850:   if (typeof a === 'string') {
851:     // Legacy codelab.json have array field as a string, for instance:
852:     // "status": "[u'ready for review']".
853:     a = JSON.parse(a.replace(/u'/, "'").replace(/'/g, '"'));
854:   }
855:   a = (a || []).filter((v) => { return (v || '').length > 0; });
856:   return a.map((v) => { return v.toLowerCase(); });
857: }
858: 
859: // sortCodelabs reorders codelabs array in-place for the given view. Pinned
860: // codelabs always come first, sorted by their pin index.
861: const sortCodelabs = (codelabs, view) => {
862:   let attr = function(codelab) {
863:     return levelledCategory(codelab, view.catLevel).name;
864:   }
865: 
866:   if (view.sort !== "mainCategory") {
867:     attr = function(codelab) { return codelab[view.sort] };
868:   }
869: 
870:   codelabs.sort(function(a, b) {
871:     // Move pinned codelabs to the top.
872:     var ia = view.pins.indexOf(a.id);
873:     var ib = view.pins.indexOf(b.id);
874:     if (ia >= 0 && ib < 0) {
875:       return -1;
876:     }
877:     if (ia < 0 && ib >= 0) {
878:       return 1;
879:     }
880:     if (ia >= 0 && ib >= 0) {
881:       return ia - ib;
882:     }
883:     // Regular sorting.
884:     var aa = attr(a);
885:     var ba = attr(b);
886:     if (aa < ba) { return -1; }
887:     if (aa > ba) { return 1; }
888:     return 0;
889:   });
890: }
891: 
892: // copyFilteredCodelabs copies all codelabs that match the given id regular
893: // expression or view regular expression into the build/ folder. If no filters
894: // are specified (i.e. if codelabRe and viewRe are both undefined), then this
895: // function returns all codelabs in the codelabs directory.
896: const copyFilteredCodelabs = (dest) =>  {
897:   // No filters were specified, symlink the codelabs folder directly and save
898:   // processing.
899:   if (CODELABS_FILTER === '*' && VIEWS_FILTER === '*') {
900:     const source = path.join(CODELABS_BUILD_DIR);
901:     const target = path.join(dest, CODELABS_NAMESPACE);
902:     fs.ensureSymlinkSync(source, target, 'dir');
903:     return
904:   }
905: 
906:   const codelabs = collectCodelabs();
907: 
908:   for(let i = 0; i < codelabs.length; i++) {
909:     const codelab = codelabs[i];
910:     const source = path.join(CODELABS_BUILD_DIR, codelab.id);
911:     const target = path.join(dest, CODELABS_NAMESPACE, codelab.id);
912:     fs.ensureSymlinkSync(source, target, 'dir');
913:   }
914: };
915: 
916: // collectCodelabs collects the list of codelabs that match the given view or
917: // codelab filter.
918: const collectCodelabs = () => {
919:   const meta = collectMetadata();
920:   let codelabs = meta.codelabs;
921: 
922:   // Only select codelabs that match the given codelab ID.
923:   if (CODELABS_FILTER !== '*') {
924:     codelabs = meta.codelabs.filter((codelab) => {
925:       return codelab.id.match(CODELABS_FILTER);
926:     });
927: 
928:     if (codelabs.length === 0) {
929:       throw new Error(`no codelabs matched: ${CODELABS_FILTER}`);
930:     }
931:   }
932: 
933:   // Only select codelabs that match the given view ID.
934:   if (VIEWS_FILTER !== '*') {
935:     let views = [];
936:     Object.keys(meta.views).forEach((key) => {
937:       if (key.match(VIEWS_FILTER)) {
938:         views.push(meta.views[key]);
939:       }
940:     });
941: 
942:     if (views.length === 0) {
943:       throw new Error(`no views matched: ${VIEWS_FILTER}`);
944:     }
945: 
946:     // Iterate over each view and include codelabs for that view.
947:     let s = new Set();
948:     for(let i = 0; i < views.length; i++) {
949:       let filtered = filterCodelabs(views[i], codelabs).codelabs;
950:       s.add(...filtered);
951:     }
952:     codelabs = s.values();
953:   }
954: 
955:   // Check if we have any codelabs
956:   if (codelabs.length === 0) {
957:     throw new Error('no codelabs matched given filters');
958:   }
959: 
960:   return codelabs;
961: }

963: // publish:staging:codelabs uploads the dist folder codelabs to a staging
964: // bucket. This only uploads the codelabs, the views remain unchanged.
965: gulp.task('publish:staging:codelabs', (callback) => {
966:   const opts = { dry: DRY_RUN, deleteMissing: DELETE_MISSING };

10: # Using trace events in Java
11: <!-- ------------------------ -->
12: ## Overview 
13: Duration: 1
14: 
15: Have you ever created a stored procedure or a user-defined function in Snowflake? If you have, then you probably want to know whether it’s working well. If something goes wrong with it, you want to know what exactly is not working as expected. In other words, you are concerned about _observability_ of your code. You probably know that you can use a [logger](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/logging-tracing/logging) in your code, and that log records are stored in the [event table](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/logging-tracing/event-table-setting-up). But have you heard about [**trace events**](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/logging-tracing/tracing)? We have recently launched them in preview, and this guide explains how they can help you improve observability.
16: 
17: Unlike log records, trace events are structured. They contain named attributes which can be easily queried with SQL.
18: 
19: Please be aware that our current implementation of trace events has several limitations. Because of these limitations, we recommend using trace events in functions and procedures which are invoked _once per query_ , as in `call my_procedure();` or `select my_function();` (but **NOT** `select my_function(x) from some_table;`)
20: 
21: 
22: ### Prerequisites
23: - A Snowflake account;
24: - Some familiarity with Java;
25: - Some familiarity with [stored procedures](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/stored-procedures-java) written in Java.
26: 
27: ### What You’ll Learn 
28: - How to emit trace events from Java code;
29: - How to analyze them by querying an event table.
30: 
31: ### What You’ll Need 
32: - A Snowflake account with an event table.
33: - If you have a Snowflake account but haven't created an event table yet, you'll need an `ACCOUNTADMIN` role so that you can set up an event table.
34: 
35: ### What You’ll Build 
36: - A stored procedure which performs several operations, collects data about each operation, and records this data as a trace event.
37: - SQL queries which you can use to find those trace events in the event table, and aggregate them.
38:

127: ### What's in the input data
128: 
129: ![Visualization of the input data](assets/chart.png)
130: 
131: These are coordinates of points on a plane. There are 3 clusters of points, centered around coordinates `(1, 2)`; `(10, 20)`; and `(5, 15)`. The stored procedure we'll create in the next step will try to find these centers by invoking the [K-Means clustering](https://towardsdatascience.com/understanding-k-means-clustering-in-machine-learning-6a6e67336aa1) algorithm.
132: 
133: ### What is K-Means clustering
134: K-means clustering is an algorithm that finds groups of points in a dataset which are close to each other. It returns coordinates of “centers” of those groups - they are called “centroids”. It is an iterative process: the algorithm places each centroid at a random point, and gradually moves it. Eventually the algorithm reaches the state when centroids don’t move. It means that the algorithm has converged, and coordinates of centroids can be returned to a caller.
135: 
136: The K-means algorithm is fast, but the caller has to know the number of clusters in advance.

138: ## Setting up an event table
139: Duration: 1
140: 
141: Trace events are stored in an event table. So, let's make sure that you have one. Please run the following commands:
142: 
143: - To check if you have _any_ event table:
144: ```sql
145: show event tables;
146: ```
147: 
148: - If the previous command returns multiple rows, you'll need to check which of the event tables is active:
149: ```sql
150: show parameters like 'EVENT_TABLE' in account;
151: ```
152: 
153: - If `show event tables` doesn't return any rows, you'll need to create a new event table and make it active:
154: 
155: ```sql
156: use role ACCOUNTADMIN;
157: create or replace event table events;
158: alter account set event_table = 'java_trace_events_quickstart.public.events';
159: ```
160: 
161: - Run this query again to confirm that the event table has been created and activated:
162: 
163: ```sql
164: show parameters like 'EVENT_TABLE' in account;
165: ```

167: ## Creating a stored procedure
168: Duration: 2
169: 
170: Now, let's create our example stored procedure. It is quite long, because it does several things:
171: - Reads data from an input table;
172: - Filters out rows with missing values;
173: - Performs [K-Means clustering](https://towardsdatascience.com/understanding-k-means-clustering-in-machine-learning-6a6e67336aa1) of valid rows;
174: - Saves the output of the clustering algorithm to the output table.
175: 
176: At each step, the procedure emits a trace event containing information about that step.
177: 
178: ### Stored procedure code
179: Please run the following query. It will create a procedure named `KMEANS`:
180: 
181: ```sql
182: create or replace procedure kmeans(
183:   inputTable string, xColumn string, yColumn string,
184:   outputTable string, clusterIdColumn string, outputXColumn string, outputYColumn string,
185:   numClusters int, maxIterations int)
186: returns string
187: language java
188: packages=('com.snowflake:snowpark:latest', 'com.snowflake:telemetry:latest')
189: handler='KMeansClusterer.run'
190: as $$
191: import com.snowflake.snowpark_java.*;
192: import com.snowflake.snowpark_java.types.DataTypes;
193: import com.snowflake.snowpark_java.types.StructField;
194: import com.snowflake.snowpark_java.types.StructType;
195: import com.snowflake.telemetry.Telemetry;
196: import io.opentelemetry.api.common.AttributeKey;
197: import io.opentelemetry.api.common.Attributes;
198: import io.opentelemetry.api.common.AttributesBuilder;
199: import java.util.*;
200: import org.slf4j.Logger;
201: import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
202: 
203: /** Performs K-Means clustering of points in 2-dimensional space. */
204: class KMeansClusterer {
205:   private static Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(KMeansClusterer.class);
206: 
207:   private static String TRACE_PREFIX = "com.mycompany.kmeans.";
208:   private static String RUNTIME_ATTR_NAME = "runtime_millis";
209: 
210:   static class Point {
211:     Point(double x, double y) {
212:       this.x = x;
213:       this.y = y;
214:     }
215: 
216:     public double getX() { return x; }
217:     
218:     public void setX(double newValue) { this.x = newValue; }
219: 
220:     public double getY() { return y; }
221: 
222:     public void setY(double newValue) { this.y = newValue; }
223: 
224:     private double x;
225:     private double y;
226:   }
227: 
228:   KMeansClusterer(
229:       Session session,
230:       String inputTableName,
231:       String xColumnName,
232:       String yColumnName,
233:       String outputTableName,
234:       String outputClusterIdColumnName,
235:       String outputXColumnName,
236:       String outputYColumnName,
237:       int numClusters,
238:       int maxIterations) {
239:     this.numClusters = numClusters;
240:     this.maxIterations = maxIterations;
241:     this.session = session;
242:     this.inputTableName = inputTableName;
243:     this.xColumnName = xColumnName;
244:     this.yColumnName = yColumnName;
245:     this.outputTableName = outputTableName;
246:     this.outputClusterIdColumnName = outputClusterIdColumnName;
247:     this.outputXColumnName = outputXColumnName;
248:     this.outputYColumnName = outputYColumnName;
249:   }
250: 
251:   /**
252:    * Performs K-Means clustering of points stored in the given input table. Stores coordinates of
253:    * clusters' centroids in the given output table.
254:    *
255:    * @param session Snowpark session
256:    * @param inputTable Name of the input table
257:    * @param xColumn Name of the column in the input table that contains X coordinates of points
258:    * @param yColumn Name of the column in the input table that contains Y coordinates of points
259:    * @param outputTableName Name of the output table
260:    * @param outputClusterIdColumnName Name of the column in the output table that will be populated
261:    *     with cluster ids. Cluster ids are integer numbers.
262:    * @param outputXColumnName Name of the column in the output table that will be populated with X
263:    *     coordinates of clusters' centroids.
264:    * @param outputYColumnName Name of the column in the output table that will be populated with Y
265:    *     coordinates of clusters' centroids.
266:    * @param numClusters Number of clusters.
267:    * @param maxIterations The limit on the number of iterations.
268:    * @return "SUCCESS" if the algorithm converged, an error message otherwise.
269:    */
270:   public static String run(
271:       Session session,
272:       String inputTable,
273:       String xColumn,
274:       String yColumn,
275:       String outputTableName,
276:       String outputClusterIdColumnName,
277:       String outputXColumnName,
278:       String outputYColumnName,
279:       int numClusters,
280:       int maxIterations) {
281:     long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
282:     AttributesBuilder attributesBuilder = Attributes.builder();
283:     String result;
284:     boolean ranClustering = false;
285: 
286:     Telemetry.setSpanAttribute(TRACE_PREFIX + "input.num_clusters", numClusters);
287:     Telemetry.setSpanAttribute(TRACE_PREFIX + "input.max_iterations", maxIterations);
288: 
289:     if (numClusters != 0) {
290:       KMeansClusterer clusterer =
291:           new KMeansClusterer(
292:               session,
293:               inputTable,
294:               xColumn,
295:               yColumn,
296:               outputTableName,
297:               outputClusterIdColumnName,
298:               outputXColumnName,
299:               outputYColumnName,
300:               numClusters,
301:               maxIterations);
302: 
303:       Row[] rows = clusterer.readInputData();
304: 
305:       if (rows.length >= numClusters) {
306:         ranClustering = true;
307:         clusterer.initializeCentroids(rows);
308:         boolean converged = clusterer.computeClusters(rows);
309:         attributesBuilder.put(AttributeKey.longKey(TRACE_PREFIX + "rows.processed"), rows.length);
310:         if (converged) {
311:           clusterer.saveCentroids();
312:           result = "SUCCESS";
313:         } else {
314:           result = "Failed to converge";
315:         }
316:       } else {
317:         result =
318:             String.format(
319:                 "Number of rows (%d) is less than the requested number of clusters (%d)",
320:                 rows.length, numClusters);
321:       }
322:     } else {
323:       result = "The number of clusters should be greater than 0";
324:     }
325: 
326:     long endTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
327:     attributesBuilder.put(AttributeKey.booleanKey(TRACE_PREFIX + "ran_clustering"), ranClustering);
328:     attributesBuilder.put(
329:         AttributeKey.longKey(TRACE_PREFIX + RUNTIME_ATTR_NAME), endTime - startTime);
330:     attributesBuilder.put(AttributeKey.stringKey(TRACE_PREFIX + "return_value"), result);
331:     Telemetry.addEvent(TRACE_PREFIX + "summary", attributesBuilder.build());
332:     logger.info(String.format("Return value: %s", result));
333:     return result;
334:   }
335: 
336:   /** Computes a distance between two points. */
337:   public static double computeDistance(double x1, double y1, double x2, double y2) {
338:     double xDiff = x1 - x2;
339:     double yDiff = y1 - y2;
340:     return Math.sqrt(xDiff * xDiff + yDiff * yDiff);
341:   }
342: 
343:   private Row[] readInputData() {
344:     long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
345:     AttributesBuilder attributesBuilder = Attributes.builder();
346:     DataFrame rawInput = session.table(inputTableName);
347:     long totalNumRows = rawInput.count();
348: 
349:     Row[] result =
350:         rawInput
351:             .filter(
352:                 Functions.col(xColumnName)
353:                     .is_not_null()
354:                     .and(Functions.not(Functions.col(xColumnName).equal_nan()))
355:                     .and(Functions.col(yColumnName).is_not_null())
356:                     .and(Functions.not(Functions.col(yColumnName).equal_nan())))
357:             .collect();
358: 
359:     long endTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
360:     long numGoodRows = result.length;
361:     long numFilteredOutRows = totalNumRows - numGoodRows;
362:     attributesBuilder.put(AttributeKey.longKey(TRACE_PREFIX + "rows.total"), totalNumRows);
363:     attributesBuilder.put(
364:         AttributeKey.longKey(TRACE_PREFIX + "rows.filtered_out"), numFilteredOutRows);
365:     attributesBuilder.put(AttributeKey.longKey(TRACE_PREFIX + "rows.good"), numGoodRows);
366:     attributesBuilder.put(
367:         AttributeKey.longKey(TRACE_PREFIX + RUNTIME_ATTR_NAME), endTime - startTime);
368:     Telemetry.addEvent(TRACE_PREFIX + "io.read", attributesBuilder.build());
369:     logger.info(
370:         String.format(
371:             "Read %d rows from input; filtered out %d of them. The remaining %d are good",
372:             totalNumRows, numFilteredOutRows, numGoodRows));
373:     return result;
374:   }
375: 
376:   private boolean computeClusters(Row[] rows) {
377:     long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
378:     AttributesBuilder attributesBuilder = Attributes.builder();
379:     int numIterations = 0;
380:     boolean centroidsMoved = true;
381: 
382:     while (centroidsMoved && numIterations < maxIterations) {
383:       computedClusters = new HashMap<>();
384:       for (Row row : rows) {
385:         double x = row.getDouble(0);
386:         double y = row.getDouble(1);
387: 
388:         double minDistance = Double.MAX_VALUE;

395:             minDistance = distance;
396:             clusterWithMinDistance = clusterId;
397:           }
398:         }
399:         if (!computedClusters.containsKey(clusterWithMinDistance)) {
400:           computedClusters.put(clusterWithMinDistance, new ArrayList<>());
401:         }
402:         computedClusters.get(clusterWithMinDistance).add(new Point(x, y));
403:       }
404: 
405:       centroidsMoved = false;
406:       for (Integer clusterId : computedClusters.keySet()) {
407:         double sumX = 0.0;
408:         double sumY = 0.0;
409:         int numPoints = 0;
410:         Point centroid = centroids.get(clusterId);
411:         for (Point pt : computedClusters.get(clusterId)) {
412:           sumX += pt.getX();
413:           sumY += pt.getY();
414:           numPoints++;
415:         }
416:         if (numPoints != 0) {
417:           double meanX = sumX / numPoints;
418:           double meanY = sumY / numPoints;
419:           double distance = computeDistance(centroid.getX(), centroid.getY(), meanX, meanY);
420:           logger.info(

423:           if (distance > 0) {
